_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: a new conversation is a selected draft row from the start. Conversation {{OTHER}} (slug {{OTHER_SLUG}}) exists. Requests to /api/conversations/draft are held before the server sees them until call "send-draft", and their answers after until call "release-draft"; the conversation the first one made is the held "draft". Call "delete-draft" deletes that conversation from outside the page. The viewport is 1280x720. The page has helpers, from an init script, used in evals: __ncHeld(name), __ncStreamed(name), __ncComposerRows(name), __ncActiveIsHeld(name), __ncHeldRows(name), __ncNoteNext(id) and __ncRecordFrames(); evals that call them return strings, and those taking a name are async: write them as given. "The active row" is ".drawer .conversation-item.active"; any check of the active row (or of something in it) starts by checking that there is exactly one (assert_count 1), as the old test's locator was strict. "The placeholder" is ".drawer [data-conversation-id='composer']". "The row of <id>" is ".drawer .conversation-item[data-conversation-id='<id>']". A row's "preview" is its ".conversation-preview" and its "title" its ".conversation-title". "The input" is data-testid "message-input", and "the Send button" data-testid "send-button". To "open a new conversation": navigate to /new, wait up to 30s for the input to be visible, and check that the active row's data-conversation-id is exactly "composer". To "start a new conversation from the header": click {"selector": ".header", "role": "button", "name": "New Conversation", "exact": true} if it is visible (it is at this size); only if it is not, click the button "More options" and then {"selector": ".chat-overflow-popover", "role": "button", "name": "New Conversation", "exact": true}. "The Delete button of the active row" is {"selector": ".drawer .conversation-item.active", "role": "button", "name": "Delete", "exact": true}. To "delete row R" (R a selector): click {"selector": R, "role": "button", "name": "Delete", "exact": true}, then click {"selector": R + " .drawer-delete-confirm", "role": "button", "name": "Delete"}. "It opened the noted row" means: assert_count 1 of the active row; eval with expect "true" of String(document.querySelector(".drawer .conversation-item.active")?.getAttribute("data-conversation-id") === window.__ncNext); the URL contains "/c/" (assert_url with text). Every selector you need is given here, so do not explore the source code or read other tests (the old Playwright spec is being replaced and does not apply): write all the steps in one run_steps call right away, and look something up only if a step fails. Perform the numbered steps in order, each fully. A button "X" is {"role": "button", "name": "X", "exact": true}, with a "selector" to scope it when it is a row's, a menu's or a group's; but "there is no button X" counts {"role": "button", "name": "X"} without exact, so that a name containing X counts too. Texts that "are exactly [...]" are checked with assert_texts. "There is no S", "no S" or "none" means no element matches at all: assert_count 0, never a visibility check. Whether an element "has the class X" is an eval of its classList.contains('X') (polled with expect), never a visibility check: a collapsed drawer may have no size. 1. Navigate to /c/{{OTHER_SLUG}} and wait up to 30s for the input to be visible. 2. The row of {{OTHER}} has the class active. 3. Start a new conversation from the header. 4. The active row's data-conversation-id is exactly "composer". 5. The active row's title matches /^draft( \d+)?$/: eval with expect "true" of String(/^draft( \d+)?$/.test(document.querySelector(".drawer .conversation-item.active .conversation-title").textContent.trim())). 6. Click the row of {{OTHER}}. 7. The row of {{OTHER}} has the class active. 8. The placeholder's count is exactly 1, and it does not have the class active. 9. Move the pointer out of the drawer: hover at x 900, y 400 of the viewport (no selector). 10. There is no placeholder (assert_count 0). 11. Start a new conversation from the header. 12. The active row's data-conversation-id is exactly "composer". 13. Fill the input with "write a limerick". 14. The active row's preview reads exactly "write a limerick". 15. Call "send-draft". 16. The event stream reported the draft before its answer came back: eval with expect "true" of __ncStreamed("draft"). 17. Still one row: eval with expect "1" of __ncComposerRows("draft"). 18. The active row's preview reads exactly "write a limerick". 19. Call "release-draft". 20. The active row is the draft's: eval with expect "true" of __ncActiveIsHeld("draft"). 21. The active row's preview reads exactly "write a limerick". 22. There is exactly one active row (assert_count 1). 23. Call "delete-draft" (no expect: it acts once). 24. The draft's row goes: eval with expect "0" of __ncHeldRows("draft").
